criteria.quote: Ponyta Is Born Without Its Signature Fire
criteria.revision: Change the title to “Ponyta’s Fiery Mane and Tail Are Missing at Birth” to create the same surprise without implying that Ponyta is born without fire itself.

criteria.quote: At birth, this Fire Horse can barely stand, with no mane or tail.
criteria.revision: Make the newborn detail more specific: “At birth, Ponyta is a weak foal that can barely stand—and it still lacks its fiery mane and tail.”

criteria.quote: What changes during Ponyta's first hour?
criteria.revision: Make the question more precise and curiosity-driven: “Does Ponyta have its iconic look at birth—or only after its first hour?”

criteria.quote: A one-hour countdown marks when the missing fire appears.
criteria.revision: Replace the countdown repetition with an evidence-based escalation: first establish that the newborn can barely stand, then reveal that its fiery mane and tail develop about an hour later.

criteria.quote: Newborn Ponyta lack their fiery mane and tail, which grow out about one hour after birth.
criteria.revision: Delay the exact timing until the reveal. Open with Ponyta lacking its recognizable mane and tail, then reveal: “About an hour after birth, they grow out and give it an impressive appearance.”

criteria.quote: BORN WITHOUT FIRE / A PLAIN FOAL / COUNTDOWN TO FIRE / THE FLAMES GROW OUT
criteria.revision: Remove the repeated absence-and-arrival beats. Give each scene a distinct fact: newborn Ponyta can barely stand, it lacks its fiery mane and tail, those features develop about an hour later, and they give it an impressive appearance.

criteria.quote: About an hour after birth, Ponyta gains the fiery mane and tail behind its impressive appearance.
criteria.revision: Make the ending connect the appearance reveal to the newborn contrast: “Ponyta begins as a foal that can barely stand and lacks its fiery look; about an hour later, the mane and tail develop and give it an impressive appearance.”

criteria.quote: Which look wins: plain foal or fiery Ponyta?
criteria.revision: Use a question that stays tied to the researched reveal: “Which is more surprising: Ponyta being barely able to stand at birth, or its fiery mane and tail appearing about an hour later?”
